chunks.arabic_text: إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، الدَّعْبَلِيُّ (ابْنُ أَخِي دَعْبَلٍ). كَانَ بِوَاسِطَ مَقَامُهُ، وَوَلِيَ الْحِسْبَةَ بِهَا. كَانَ كَذَّابًا وَضَاعًا لِلْحَدِيثِ، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَى مَا رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ الرِّضَا (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) وَلَا غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ، وَلَا مَا صَنَّفَ.

translations.en: Ismāʿīl b. ʿAlī b. ʿAlī, al-Diʿbilī [ibn Akhī Diʿbil]. He resided in Wāsiṭ, and was responsible for its treasury. He was a liar, fabricator of ḥadīths. What he narrates from his father from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) is not regarded, nor is other than that (to be regarded), nor what he authored.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ* highlights Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī al-Diʿbilī, a resident of Wāsiṭ who served as the city's *ḥāṣib* (market inspector), yet was deemed unreliable (*thiqa* in position but weak in transmission). His narrations from Imam al-Riḍā (AS) and his own compositions are rejected due to his tendency toward fabrication (*kadhdhāb*) and negligence in preserving hadith, illustrating the critical Shia methodology of distinguishing between administrative status and scholarly integrity.
en.seo_question: Who was Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī al-Diʿbilī and what was his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.الدَّعْبَلِيُّ: al-Diʿbilī (a nisba indicating relation to the Banu Diʿbal tribe or family)
key_terms.الْحِسْبَةَ: al-ḥisbah (the office of market inspector or treasury manager)
key_terms.ضَاعًا: ḍāʿan (one who fabricates or spoils narrations)
